---
title: "Poisson spike-train deconvolution"
description: "Recover sharp events from blurred signals, including grouped multichannel data."
output: rmarkdown::html_document
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse=TRUE, comment="#>", message=FALSE, warning=FALSE,
  fig.width=9, fig.height=5, dpi=144)
library(L0glm)
options(width=95, digits=3)
```

In deconvolution the design contains shifted copies of a point-spread function.
Coefficients represent sharp events, while the observed signal is blurred and
noisy. For nonnegative Poisson intensities this is an identity-link GLM:

\[
Y_i\sim\operatorname{Poisson}\{(X\beta)_i\},\qquad\beta\geq0.
\]

L0glm fits this likelihood directly. Its native `L0nnpois()` backend keeps
sparse convolution matrices sparse and shares them across multichannel OpenMP fits.

## Single channel

```{r single}
single <- simul(method=2, n=500L, p=500L, s=.1, seed=2L)
fit <- L0glm.fit(single$X, single$y, family=poisson("identity"),
  nonnegative=TRUE, lambda="gic", relaxed=TRUE, parallelize=FALSE)
L0glm.metrics(fit, beta_true=single$beta_true)[
  c("gic", "TP", "FP", "FN", "TN", "F1_score", "MCC")]
```

Compare with alternative methods using one common scoring interface:

```{r compare, eval=FALSE}
comparison <- sparseglm(single, family=poisson("identity"),
  method=c("L0glm", "abess", "lasso", "relaxed_lasso"),
  tune="gic", nlambda=10L, nonnegative=TRUE, intercept=FALSE,
  approximation="wls", support.size=seq_len(100L),
  lambda=list(L0glm=fit$init.lambda), options=list(L0glm=list(relaxed=TRUE)))
L0glm.metrics(comparison)
plot(comparison, which=c(1, 2))
```

The published example below puts the observed and true signal above zero and
mirrors each method's fitted signal and spikes below it. Separate panels make
false positives and missed events easy to see.

<img src="../deconvolution-single.png" alt="Observed and true signal above, mirrored fitted signals and spikes below, separately for L0glm, ABESS, LASSO and relaxed LASSO." width="100%">

## Multichannel row selection

For several response channels, shared event times correspond to active rows of
the coefficient matrix. Within each recovered row, channel coefficients describe
the event's spectrum.

```{r multi}
multi <- simul(method=4, n=500L, p=500L, s=.05, seed=2L)
# Retain all mass channels generated by the simulation.
fit_multi <- L0glm.fit(multi$X, multi$y, family=poisson("identity"),
  nonnegative=TRUE, lambda="gic", grouped=TRUE, relaxed=TRUE, ncores=2L)
L0glm.metrics(fit_multi, beta_true=multi$beta_true)[c("gic", "TP", "FP", "FN", "TN",
  "F1_score", "MCC", "within_row_F1_score", "within_row_MCC")]
```

Row F1 and MCC assess event-time recovery. Within-row F1 and MCC assess the
sparsity of channel coefficients among correctly recovered true-positive rows.

`plot.sparseglm()` can show all coefficients, row averages or heatmaps.
Choose methods using `which`; heatmaps display one ground-truth/estimate pair per method.

```{r heatmap-code, eval=FALSE}
comparison_multi <- sparseglm(multi, family=poisson("identity"),
  method=c("L0glm", "abess", "lasso", "relaxed_lasso"),
  tune="gic", nlambda=10L, nonnegative=TRUE, intercept=FALSE,
  approximation="wls_grouped", support.size=seq_len(50L),
  lambda=list(L0glm=fit_multi$init.lambda), options=list(L0glm=list(relaxed=TRUE)))
plot(comparison_multi, type="heatmap", which=c(1, 3))
plot(comparison_multi, type="coefs", which=1, channels="mean")
```

<img src="../deconvolution-multi-l0glm.png" alt="Ground truth and estimated multichannel coefficients for L0glm, with all channels shown." width="100%">

<img src="../deconvolution-multi-lasso.png" alt="Ground truth and estimated multichannel coefficients for LASSO, with all channels shown." width="100%">

Cyan lines identify true-positive event rows, red lines false positives, and
magenta lines false negatives. The [benchmark tables](performance.html) include
the complete comparison and the scoring conventions.

<img src="../deconvolution-coefficients.png" alt="True versus estimated coefficients across every response channel, in separate panels for each method." width="100%">

## Tune or use native validation

```{r tune, eval=FALSE}
gic <- L0glm.tune(multi$X, multi$y, family=poisson("identity"),
  tune="gic", nlambda=10, nonnegative=TRUE, grouped=TRUE, relaxed=TRUE)
cv <- L0glm.tune(multi$X, multi$y, family=poisson("identity"),
  tune="cv", nfolds=5, nlambda=10, nonnegative=TRUE, grouped=TRUE, relaxed=TRUE)
```

For held-out checkpoint stopping, supply `validation=list(X=V, y=v)`;
OpenMP remains available through the native backend. See the
[validation example](controls.html#held-out-early-stopping).

The L0 deconvolution idea is developed by
[de Rooi & Eilers (2011)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.aca.2011.05.030).
`simul()` also supports Gaussian or negative-binomial noise for blurred spike trains.
